turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided Owen's zero, and was he heard before it went into the gradebook?
You need an answer? I asked you two questions, Hale, and you've answered neither. Who decided, and was Owen heard first?
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

Admits what? My child never lies, and I'm writing down that you said "Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript." Your own procedure, 4.4, says a first concern gets a supervised reassessment and nothing on his record, so either show me something or I'm in the principal's office at 4:41.
Those are the only two options. Pick one.

"The only two options." Not under your school's procedure, Hale, and I'm not picking either. Nobody called me before that zero went in, which breaks 4.2, so what evidence do you have besides a machine?
